blocks.text: A Herbal Consultant works with knowledge of medicinal plants, traditional herbal preparations, their documented uses, quality considerations and safe handling. Depending on qualifications and local regulations, the role may involve herbal education, product research, ingredient documentation, cultivation guidance or advising organisations on herbal products.

Sowa-Rigpa is a traditional system of medicine practised in Himalayan regions and other communities. Studying Sowa-Rigpa can provide a foundation in its traditional theories, materia medica and approaches to health.

blocks.label: Important professional distinction
blocks.text: A person trained in herbal wellness is not automatically qualified to diagnose disease, prescribe medicines, practise as a registered medical practitioner or claim to treat medical conditions. Those activities depend on recognised qualifications, registration and applicable laws.

sections.heading: What does a Herbal Consultant do?

blocks.text: Typical responsibilities can include:

items.text: Identify medicinal plants using reliable botanical references and expert guidance.
Study traditional uses of herbs and distinguish them from evidence established through modern research.
Maintain records of botanical names, plant parts, sources and preparation methods.
Explain general information about herbal ingredients and traditional practices within the professional scope.
Support quality checks for raw herbs and herbal products.
Research literature on safety, contraindications and possible herb–drug interactions.
Coordinate with botanists, pharmacists, clinicians, manufacturers and quality-control teams.
Assist in documenting sourcing, storage, processing and traceability.
Support responsible labelling and consumer education.
Refer questions involving diagnosis, medication changes, pregnancy, serious symptoms or adverse reactions to qualified healthcare professionals.

blocks.text: The exact duties depend on whether the person works in education, research, manufacturing, traditional medicine or a regulated clinical setting.

blocks.label: Important
blocks.text: The programme in your career database is a pathway label, not necessarily the formal name of a recognised degree. In India, the regulated Sowa-Rigpa undergraduate qualification is called Bachelor of Sowa-Rigpa Medicine and Surgery (BSRMS). Its recognised status, admission requirements and professional registration implications should be verified with the National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (NCISM).
NCISM India

The National Institute of Sowa-Rigpa describes a 5.5-year course structure, including a compulsory 12-month rotating internship. Confirm the current admission requirements and permitted college status before applying.

blocks.text: Job titles vary by employer. Candidates should search for related roles such as herbal research assistant, medicinal-plant project assistant, pharmacognosy research associate, herbal quality-control assistant and natural-products documentation associate.
This is one of the most important parts of the career.

blocks.label: Medical practice
blocks.text: Do not assume that a short herbal course permits diagnosis, prescribing or treatment. Check the relevant qualification and registration rules.

blocks.label: Product compliance
blocks.text: Requirements depend on whether a product is regulated as an Ayurvedic, Sowa-Rigpa, other traditional medicine, food, cosmetic or another product category.

blocks.label: Evidence
blocks.text: Traditional use, laboratory studies and clinical evidence are different types of evidence and should be described accurately.

blocks.label: Interactions
blocks.text: Herbal ingredients can interact with prescribed medicines or cause adverse effects.

blocks.label: Quality
blocks.text: Contamination, adulteration, misidentification and incorrect storage can create significant risks.

blocks.label: Advertising
blocks.text: Avoid unsupported claims that an herbal product cures diseases or is safe for everyone.
For regulated Sowa-Rigpa education and professional recognition, begin with NCISM's official resources.

There is no single standard salary for a Herbal Consultant. Income depends on qualifications, location, employer, research or manufacturing specialisation, client base and the scope of permitted services.

blocks.label: Career outcome
blocks.text: A Herbal Consultant can build a career in medicinal-plant research, herbal product quality, traditional-medicine documentation or appropriately scoped wellness education. For this career pathway, scientific accuracy, product safety and clarity about professional qualifications are essential.
